`ReactDOM.render` returns the instance of the root component, but only if React has rendered it by the time the call returns. React does not promise that. To get the instance, give the root element a `ref` callback. React calls it when the instance exists.

The call is reported when its result is stored in a variable or a property, assigned, or returned.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
const app = ReactDOM.render(<App />, document.body);
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
function mount(root) {
  return ReactDOM.render(<App />, root);
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
let app;

ReactDOM.render(<App ref={instance => (app = instance)} />, document.body);
```
